# Email Newsletters for Developers: What to Send

![Developer reading a technology newsletter](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1516321318423-f06f85e504b3)

Email newsletters remain one of the most reliable ways to build an audience. Unlike social media platforms, you own your email list and can communicate directly with subscribers whenever you want.

For developers, newsletters can become a powerful channel for sharing knowledge, growing a community, promoting projects, and building trust over time.

The challenge isn't convincing people to subscribe.

The challenge is giving them a reason to keep opening your emails.

This guide explains what developers should send in a newsletter and how to keep subscribers engaged.

---

## Why Developers Should Consider a Newsletter

Many developers focus exclusively on:

- Social media
- Blog posts
- Open-source projects
- Video content

While these channels are valuable, email offers unique advantages.

Benefits include:

- Direct communication
- No algorithm dependency
- Higher engagement rates
- Better audience ownership
- Long-term relationship building

A newsletter creates a consistent connection with your audience.

---

## Start With a Clear Purpose

Before sending your first email, define the newsletter's purpose.

Examples:

### Educational Newsletter

Share:

- Tutorials
- Coding tips
- Learning resources
- Best practices

Audience:

- Students
- Junior developers
- Self-learners

---

### Industry Updates Newsletter

Share:

- Framework updates
- Browser changes
- Tool releases
- AI developments

Audience:

- Professional developers
- Tech enthusiasts

---

### Personal Journey Newsletter

Share:

- Lessons learned
- Side projects
- Challenges
- Career growth

Audience:

- Followers interested in your experience

---

### Product-Focused Newsletter

Share:

- Product updates
- Feature releases
- Community stories
- Roadmaps

Audience:

- Existing users
- Potential customers

---
